title: UN Adds Israel to Annual Blacklist for Conflict-Related Sexual Violence
detail: The United Nations added Israel to its annual blacklist of parties accused of committing sexual violence in conflict zones on May 28, 2026. The move is part of the UN Secretary-General's annual report on conflict-related sexual violence, which lists parties credibly suspected of committing or being responsible for patterns of rape and other forms of sexual violence in armed conflict. Israel's inclusion marks a significant diplomatic development and was immediately condemned by Israeli officials and allied governments as politicized and factually unfounded. UN investigators cited findings related to October 7 captives who were held in Gaza as well as reports from Palestinian detainees in Israeli custody. Human rights organizations welcomed the listing while noting it came more than two years after the conflict began.

title: IDF Kills Hamas Gaza City Brigade Deputy Commander Aslim and Northern Gaza Brigade Leader Bik in Same Strike
detail: Israeli forces struck a civilian residence in Gaza City on May 28, 2026, killing Imad Aslim — deputy commander of the Hamas Gaza City Brigade and commander of its Zeitoun Battalion — alongside Izz al-Din Bik, the commander of Hamas's Northern Gaza Brigade, in a single operation. The IDF reported both men were meeting at the location when the strike hit. In the same operational period, the IDF also separately confirmed the killing of Ihad Khreizim, a Hamas financier responsible for 'millions of dollars' in Qassam Brigades funding, and Muhammad al-Habash, who commanded a Hamas weapons production headquarters. The confirmation of Aslim and Bik's deaths — reported by the Times of Israel liveblog on May 29 — represented the elimination of two mid-to-senior Hamas brigade commanders in a single strike, continuing the rapid attrition of Hamas's command and control infrastructure following the elimination of two successive Qassam Brigades chiefs (al-Haddad on May 15 and Odeh on May 26). The Foundation for Defense of Democracies catalogued these killings as part of a broader campaign in which the IDF reported 10 ceasefire violations between May 21-28.

media.caption: IDF kills Hamas Gaza City Brigade deputy commander Aslim and Northern Gaza Brigade leader Bik in same strike — May 28, 2026

title: IDF Confirms Killing Hamas Financier Khreizim and Weapons Production Chief Habash
detail: The IDF confirmed on May 28, 2026 the killing of Ihad Khreizim, a Hamas financier described by Israeli military intelligence as responsible for channeling 'millions of dollars' to the Qassam Brigades' operational structure. Separately, the IDF confirmed the killing of Muhammad al-Habash, identified as leading a Hamas weapons manufacturing headquarters responsible for producing rockets, explosives, and improvised weapons for use against Israeli forces and civilians. Both killings were part of Israel's sustained campaign to degrade Hamas's military and financial infrastructure beyond leadership strikes. The IDF's intelligence directorate (Aman) tracked both figures as central nodes in the weapons production and funding network that sustained Hamas's capacity to resist Israeli operations. These confirmations came on the same day the IDF reported killing two Hamas brigade-level commanders (Aslim and Bik), representing a notably high-intensity intelligence and strike tempo in a single 24-hour period.

media.caption: IDF kills Hamas financier Khreizim and weapons production chief Habash — May 28, 2026 (FDD Analysis)
